head: d91d30d4af51bc67317ef8afc0b46b1dbef94038
doctrine: A MEMBER WITH NO CHANNEL OF ITS OWN IS NAMED, NOT SMUGGLED. Each row states: own store / own schema / own verbs / own channel / what it rides / plan membership.

members.own_store: YES - storeKey 'water', inline ALL_PLUGINS descriptor in apps/editor/src/PluginRegistry.ts (id 'water', storeKey 'water')
members.own_verbs: NONE - declared exempt in STORE_ONLY_PLUGIN_IDS: 'ADR-0124 s4 - water is created and destroyed only by pool.* ; it owns no verb of its own.'
members.own_channel: YES - 'water.created', emitted inside the CEB pool.create case. 1 subscriber: initTools.ts:1943 (FT-WATER). Registers in VDT (:1982) and bimManager (:1984) and REFUSES to register on an empty levelId.
members.rides: nothing - it has its own channel
members.plan: NO - 'water' is absent from GEOMETRY_ELEMENT_TYPES (21-member set, re-measured 2026-08-31). 3D only.
members.verdict: NAMED, NOT SMUGGLED. The strongest member row in the repo: own store, own schema, own channel, and a WRITTEN reason for owning no verb.

members.own_store: NO - they ARE walls, written into the wall store
members.rides: 'wall.created', restamped by the CEB pool.create case, guarded on wall.parentId === p.poolId, commandType kept as 'pool.create'
members.verdict: RIDES A PARENT CHANNEL, DECLARED. CommandEventBridge.ts states its refusal to smuggle the water onto slab.created in its own words (C84 EI-9).

members.rides: 'element.updated' (elementKind 'slab', changedFields ['holes']), emitted ONLY when the replace patch is actually on the commit
members.verdict: RIDES A PARENT CHANNEL, DECLARED. This is the only compound MUTATION in the repo measured to reach a mirror.

members.own_store: YES - storeKey 'liftPart', its own inline ALL_PLUGINS descriptor
members.own_schema: NO - there is no LiftPart.ts in packages/schemas/src/elements/
members.own_verbs: NONE - declared exempt in STORE_ONLY_PLUGIN_IDS (C104 s2)
members.rides: the PARENT's 'lift.created'. Parts travel as ev.parts[] and are drawn by liftCompoundMeshBuilder.updateLift (initTools.ts:1687-1701). initTools.ts:1665 states liftPart 'has no legacy store to mirror INTO - liftPart is a new family (C104 R-3)'.
members.plan: NO. 'liftPart' is not in GEOMETRY_ELEMENT_TYPES. 'verticalCirculation' IS - but that is the OTHER lift (the LOD-200 massing lift in @pryzm/geometry-lift), not this compound.
members.verdict: NAMED, RIDES PARENT. There is NO 'lift.deleted' key in RuntimeEvents - stated by apps/editor/src/engine/bathroomPodMemberMirror.ts:30-32 as the reason the lift had to hand-build a render sink. So lift.delete (UNKNOWN liveness) has no channel to relay on, for the parent or the parts.

members.own_verbs: NONE - no landing verb exists among the 361
members.rides: nothing on the bus - it is built by StairMeshBuilder from the parent stair (declaredProjectScopes.ts:661)
members.plan: CLAIMED AND DEAD. 'stair-landing' IS in GEOMETRY_ELEMENT_TYPES (ViewDependencyTracker.ts:82), but StairLandingStore emits the CAMEL-CASE spelling. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-31: StairLandingStore.ts:42/66/90 all emit elementType:'stairLanding'. The hyphenated member matches nothing.
members.verdict: DEAD ENTRY - AND THE CODE SAYS SO FIRST. ViewDependencyTracker.ts:66-79 declares it a 'MEASURED DEAD ENTRY' and explains it is left in place deliberately, because correcting the spelling without a registerElement site first would route a 31-segment railing run into 31 G3-STALE all-views sweeps. I re-measured; it holds. This is an HONEST declaration, not a stale one.

members.own_verbs: ONE, AND IT IS ON THE PARENT'S PREFIX - 'stair.createRailing' (LIVE, via the legacy commandManager). There is no stair-railing.* verb, and no railing delete or update verb anywhere.
members.plan: CLAIMED AND DEAD - same mechanism as stair-landing. RE-MEASURED: StairRailingStore.ts:70/97/115/126 emit 'stairRailing'.
members.verdict: DEAD ENTRY (declared) PLUS A THREE-WAY REPRESENTATION SPLIT. A railing exists as (a) the verb stair.createRailing, (b) the store key 'stair-railing', and (c) the entirely separate top-level FAMILY 'handrail'. Three vocabularies for one physical thing.

members.parent: listed by the brief under stair - MEASURED, it is a TOP-LEVEL family
members.own_store: YES - storeKey 'handrail', its own inline ALL_PLUGINS descriptor
members.verdict: NOT A MEMBER - A FULL FAMILY. Recorded here because the brief listed it as a stair member. Measured, it is independent of the stair, and it is the third rival to 'railing' above.

members.parent: plumbing (the DESCRIPTOR that registers its two verbs)
members.own_store: YES - storeKey 'bathroomPod', its own inline ALL_PLUGINS descriptor
members.own_verbs: TWO - bathroomPod.create, bathroomPod.delete. BOTH UNKNOWN liveness. STORE_ONLY_PLUGIN_IDS carries a written note that this exemption's reason DIFFERS from water's and liftPart's, because the pod DOES own verbs; they are simply registered by the plumbing descriptor (a descriptor carries exactly one storeKey).
members.own_channel: NO - there is no CEB case and no *.created event for the pod or its members.
members.rides: NOTHING ON THE BUS. Members are projected into the LEGACY @pryzm/geometry-plumbing fixture store through Store.subscribeDirty() - apps/editor/src/engine/bathroomPodMemberMirror.ts, attached at initTools.ts:1758. ctx.stores.plumbing is a DIFFERENT store (the plugin DTO pipe store); the mirror header states this explicitly.
members.plan: members YES via plumbing; the POD ITSELF is deliberately not drawn (C109 s1)
members.verdict: NAMED, AND THE ONLY MEMBER SET THAT USES A STORE SUBSCRIPTION RATHER THAN A CHANNEL - which is why create, undo, redo and delete all arrive through ONE road and cannot drift. Its own header names what it does NOT close: ProjectSerializer knows nothing about pods, so a save-and-reload keeps every MEMBER and LOSES THE PARENT (childrenIds, drill-in and delete-reap do not survive). L-11485 OPEN: there is no bathroomPod.update verb, and minting one blindly would silently discard an architect's plumbing.move.

members.own_schema: PARTIAL - packages/schemas/src/elements/CurtainPanelVocabulary.ts is a VOCABULARY file, not a defineElement row
members.own_verbs: NONE OF ITS OWN. All seven panel verbs carry the PARENT prefix: curtain-wall.addPanel, .removePanel, .replacePanel, .swapPanel, .rotatePanel, .bulkUpdatePanels, .setPanelType
members.verdict: RIDES PARENT. It has a store AND a plan membership but no verb and no channel of its own - addressable as geometry and as a plan symbol, never as a command subject.

members.own_verbs: NONE OF ITS OWN - only curtain-wall.setMullionType and curtain-wall.setTransomType
members.plan: no type key of its own
members.verdict: FULLY SUBSUMED. Named because the brief asked. There is no mullion element anywhere in the census - not a store, not a schema, not a type key, not a verb subject. It exists only as a TYPE-ID PROPERTY of its parent. That is a defensible design, but it is a fact nobody had written down.

members.own_store: YES - initStores.ts r('opening', ...). openingStore is read directly by packages/command-registry/src/stair/DeleteStairCommand.ts:349
members.own_schema: NO - there is no Opening.ts in packages/schemas/src/elements/
members.own_verbs: THREE CREATE VERBS, AND NOTHING ELSE. 'opening.create' (LIVE, owner apps/editor, routed through the legacy commandManager), 'wall.createOpening' (UNKNOWN, plugins/wall), 'wall.opening.create' (UNKNOWN, plugins/wall). There is NO opening.delete, NO opening.update and NO opening.move among the 361.
members.own_channel: YES - 'wall.opening.created', 2 subscribers (initTools.ts:1530 among them). TWO CEB cases feed it: :721 wall.opening.create and :731 wall.createOpening.
members.rides: nothing - it has its own channel
members.verdict: THE RIVAL ROW. Three creation verbs on TWO different execution authorities for one member, and zero verbs for the whole rest of its lifecycle. Deletion is reached only indirectly - through DeleteStairCommand's auto-opening cascade (legacy) and OpeningDeleteConsequencePlanner. Minting an opening.delete without first collapsing the three creates would make it a fourth rival, not a fix.
